name: Rendezvous
award: 2023 Federal 4% and state housing tax credits (Round Two)
headline: Volunteers of America National Services combined a renovation of the 30-unit Pavilion Gardens (converted from family to senior housing) with a new 22-unit building to create Rendezvous, 52 apartments for adults 55+ at 30% to 60% AMI on VOA's Montrose senior campus; it won 2023 Round Two federal 4% and state credits with $10.96M of CHFA bonds, closed and broke ground in October 2024 and opened in September 2025.
why_it_matters: It shows how a nonprofit can reposition an under-occupied rural family property into senior housing next to its existing services, using short-term bonds with no permanent bond debt, a foundation PRI in place of a taxable tail, a $2.6M CDBG grant passed through the city and housing authority vouchers and tax exemption.

status.label: Complete and open (grand opening 2025-09-24)
status.detail: VOANS closed its financing and broke ground in October 2024; the grand opening was held on 2025-09-24, and on 2026-02-03 Montrose City Council held the CDBG closeout hearing, with staff reporting the acquisition completed and renovations finalized.

next_step: Watch for CHFA placed-in-service and compliance records and the planned future 44-unit phase on the adjacent land.

key_numbers.meaning: 28 one-bedroom and 24 two-bedroom units for ages 55+ at 30% to 60% AMI (income average 50%); 30 renovated, 22 new.
About $9.6M over 10 years, plus $1,100,000 of state credit.
Short-term privately placed tax-exempt bonds only; no long-term bonds, with VOA committed to take out the bonds with a below-market loan.
Includes $4.6M from the State Housing Board in 2024: a $2.6M CDBG grant through the City of Montrose and a $2M Division of Housing loan request.

facts.value: 2366 Robins Way, Montrose 81401 (the city spells it Robbins Way)
N, A/R; S: new construction plus acquisition/rehab, senior
Pavilion Gardens, 30 family units at 50% and 60% AMI built in 2000 in nine one-story and townhome-style buildings, owned by a VOA entity for more than 10 years

Twelve two-story three-bedroom units converted to one-story two-bedroom units with a closet replacing the stairs; interiors matched to the new building; playground and basketball court replaced by a pickleball court and seating

Two-story, elevator-served, 22 trauma-informed-design units on an adjacent vacant lot (the application gives both 1.97 acres and a 1.16-acre lot), wood frame on micropiles, electrification-ready; Enterprise Green Communities, WELL and Energy Star targets
Pavilion Gardens lot R-3A; new lot rezoned to R-4 in 2020, allowing 22 units; subdivision complete before application
Eight project-based vouchers from the Montrose County Housing Authority
Montrose County Housing Authority to serve as special limited partner for the exemption, per the application
Part-time services coordinator; VOA Montrose campus with two Section 202 senior properties, assisted living, a PACE center and the senior center nearby
Non-metro county priority (Montrose County population 43,811); Difficult Development Area status cited as a reason to win in 2023

money.note: CHFA issuer, privately placed, short-term only; cap requested from CHFA, noting Montrose County has transferred its cap to CHFA in recent years.

money.source: Community Development Block Grant (via City of Montrose)
money.note: Awarded September 2024 for acquisition of the 30-unit building; the city was pass-through with no local match; closeout hearing 2026-02-03.
Part of $4.6M the State Housing Board awarded for Rendezvous in 2024.
US Bank equity and construction loan.

money.source: Other sources named in the application
money.note: Colorado Health Foundation PRI construction loan instead of a taxable tail; VOA carryback loans and existing VOA subordinate loan (over $500K); $750K VOA Capital Magnet Fund loan; deferred fee; about $50K city fee waivers. Existing CHFA and HOME loans to be paid off.

background.text: Rendezvous competed unsuccessfully in the 2021 9% round and was restructured as a 4% plus state credit deal on CHFA's feedback.

Pavilion Gardens struggled with occupancy as a family property surrounded by senior housing (about 10% vacancy), which drove the conversion to senior units; the state noted the property's history of struggling with occupancy.

About 13 households who did not meet the age rule needed permanent relocation under the Uniform Relocation Act; VOA planned to coordinate moves to a nearby new family tax credit development and to cover any relocation costs above budget.
The market study gave a 13.3% overall capture rate; the one comparable senior tax credit property had a waitlist of over 486 households.
VOA plans a future phase of about 44 more units next to the new building.
The applicant requested a cost basis waiver.

timeline.event: Pavilion Gardens opens as a family property
Adjacent vacant lot rezoned to R-4
CHFA announces 2023 Round Two awards, including Rendezvous
VOA presents the project to the State Housing Board
City of Montrose awarded $2.6M CDBG for the project
City Council holds CDBG closeout hearing

discrepancies.text: In 2024 the state documents put the cost at $22.28 million, while the 2025 opening coverage calls it a $23 million investment.
VOA Colorado's property page describes Rendezvous as 22 apartments, while CHFA and the opening announcements count 52.
VOANS gives the income range as about $20,000 to $45,000, while the 2025 opening coverage gives $21,000 to $49,000.
